scope: Metadata-only primary-literature and official-test-method review for fired earthenware and porcelain stoneware comparators. No physical tests or production-parameter updates were made.

local_reference_files.role: Existing local secondary research note used to avoid duplicating prior Kalami and Kilikoglou coverage; not a primary paper file.

source_file_hash_policy: No primary-source PDF or ASTM standard was mirrored locally because this assignment allows only three metadata outputs. Each source record therefore sets localfilehash to null; no URL digest is misrepresented as a local file hash.

sources.citation: N. S. Müller, G. Vekinis, P. M. Day, and V. Kilikoglou, The influence of microstructure and texture on the mechanical properties of rock tempered archaeological ceramics, Journal of the European Ceramic Society 35 (2015), 831-843.
sources.verification: Primary author-hosted PDF opened and inspected; paper pages 832-839 were checked for sample manufacture, water-immersion porosity, strength, notched fracture, modulus, and summary values.

source_partial_coverage.condition: Un-tempered low-calcareous Kalami experimental clay briquette fired at 1050 C, plus other clay/firing/temper states as contrasts.
covered: Firing schedule: 200 C/h, 1 h soak, air; ambient drying for >10 days before firing.
Total porosity about 11%, mainly closed; companion material total porosity method and stated approx. +/-2% uncertainty.
Three-point TRS about 70 MPa (five measurements; support span and numeric scatter unavailable).
Effective finite-notch mode-I K about 1.2 MPa m^1/2 (four-point notched bend, n=3); G is related to K and E in paper.
not_covered_or_not_reported: Fired bulk density value; the 2.77 +/- 0.05 g/mL figure is estimated true density of raw Kalami clay, not fired bulk density.
Poisson ratio, direct tensile strength, numerical per-specimen spread for the 1.2 MPa m^1/2 value, and measured moisture at test.
A project-specific full material card or calibration for archaeological sherds.

sources.citation: J. Martín-Márquez, J. M. Rincón, and M. Romero, Effect of microstructure on mechanical properties of porcelain stoneware, Journal of the European Ceramic Society 30 (2010), 3063-3069.
sources.verification: Primary article metadata and author-manuscript text were checked via the journal record and repository-indexed full text, including Table 2 and the methods extract.

source_partial_coverage.condition: Reference industrial tile body: 50 wt% kaolinitic clay, 40 wt% feldspar, 10 wt% quartz; fast-fired from 1200 to 1300 C.
covered: Dynamic E by resonance-frequency method; table gives 48-65 GPa by firing temperature.
Indentation-derived K_Ic values 1.2-1.4 MPa m^1/2; 1000 gf, 15 s, ten-indentation mean per condition, with no SD tabulated.
Flexural test: UNE-EN 843-1, 50 x 10 x 8 mm bars, 36 mm span, 3 mm/min, n=10.
Bulk/open/absolute density and porosity methods are named (ASTM C373-88 and C329-88); results are plotted rather than numerically tabulated in the extracted article text.
not_covered_or_not_reported: Poisson ratio, direct tensile strength, and a sharp-precracked mode-I K_Ic or measured G_c.
Per-temperature flexural strength means and dispersions in a tabulated form.
Residual moisture or controlled humidity at mechanical test.

sources.citation: ASTM C1421-18(2025), Standard Test Methods for Determination of Fracture Toughness of Advanced Ceramics at Ambient Temperature.
sources.verification: ASTM International official standard page; active edition and scope inspected.

covered: Mode-I fracture-toughness methods for precracked beam, surface crack in flexure, and chevron-notched beam specimens at ambient temperature.
Sharp-crack beam methods, reporting in SI units, and sensitivity of reported values to crack method, environment, rate, and temperature.
not_covered_or_not_reported: No ceramic-body property numbers or project material qualification.
Advanced-ceramic scope does not establish direct applicability to porous or tempered traditional pottery.

sources.citation: ASTM C1259-21(2026), Standard Test Method for Dynamic Young’s Modulus, Shear Modulus, and Poisson’s Ratio for Advanced Ceramics by Impulse Excitation of Vibration.
sources.verification: ASTM International official standard page; active version, method title, and measurement scope inspected.

covered: Dynamic E from flexural resonance and shear modulus from torsional resonance; nu is computed from the elastic moduli.
not_covered_or_not_reported: No ceramic-body property numbers or project material qualification.
Dynamic values do not automatically equal static moduli for a fracture solver; scope is advanced ceramics.
